title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 24, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: langchain-ai/langchain is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: langchain-ai/langchain leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: langchain-ai/langchain — 1 commit today and 1 same-day mapped article, 5.1 below its current daily pace, with 3 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 220 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 386 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Try old recipes before embedding the lean Goose build
dailyInsight.insight: Goose's merged lean ACP executable gives application teams a smaller build target, but existing recipe declarations can request extensions that target omits.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The lean build disables tree-sitter and its analyze registration. The recipe parser still injects analyze for an older built-in developer declaration; a public review traces the resulting extension-load failure, which the author accepts.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A successful package-size check does not prove that imported agent configurations will load. Embedders need an explicit compatibility policy for the feature set they ship.

actions.audience: Application teams evaluating Goose's lean ACP binary
actions.label: Check representative recipes against the pinned feature set
actions.instruction: In an isolated integration environment, pin the Goose revision and build features, then try representative existing recipes, including a legacy built-in developer declaration. Record which extensions load and which are explicitly rejected. Compare with the normal build before changing any bundled runtime.
actions.effort: One focused integration session after building both configurations

receipts.title: Merged lean ACP executable and feature gates
receipts.supports: Defines the no-default-features lean target, conditional analyze registration and platform-specific size budget.

receipts.title: Legacy recipe compatibility review
receipts.supports: Traces automatic analyze injection to a missing-extension failure in the lean configuration.

confidence.basis: The recipe parser and conditional extension registry agree with the specific public review; the author explicitly accepts this compatibility boundary.

dailyInsight.limitation: We did not compile the binary, independently reproduce the recipe failure, measure its size or verify a released lean artifact. The ordinary full build is a different configuration.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the recipe warning if the shipped lean configuration includes analyze or its recipe-loading path demonstrably handles legacy developer declarations without requesting an unavailable extension.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A pinned distributable lean artifact and migration tests that show how old recipes and agent settings are handled.
